## README.md
# Sample Earth: Tree Crop Reference Dataset

[![DOI](https://img.shields.io/badge/DOI-10.60480%2Fmjsk--yg88-lightgray)](https://doi.org/10.60480/mjsk-yg88)

This dataset is part of the [Sample Earth](https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/73040655-ce35-4f4e-8126-4527703cc5f3) initiative, a global effort to build open, high-quality reference data for improving the accuracy and inclusiveness of land-cover maps.

This dataset contains GPS-located land-cover samples that can be used to train and validate AI models that generate detailed, accurate maps, with a focus on coffee and cocoa production systems.  The data were collected across Colombia and Ghana through expert interpretation of high-resolution satellite imagery. Each sample is labelled and quality-controlled to represent the land-cover types. The classification scheme includes four main classes: coffee, cocoa, tree crops, and seasonal agriculture.

While the primary goal is to distinguish coffee and cocoa systems from other land uses, the dataset also supports broader applications such as agricultural monitoring, deforestation analysis, ecosystem-service mapping, land-use planning, and suitability modelling.

By providing transparent, well-validated training data, this dataset contributes to Sample Earth's broader objective: strengthening AI-based land monitoring tools and supporting global efforts, including the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), to ensure sustainable, deforestation-free agricultural supply chains.

The dataset is designed to grow continuously, incorporating new commodities, timeframes, and countries over time.

This dataset was produced with the support of Google.

## Sample annotated ROI

![sample annotation](https://data.source.coop/alliance-bioversity-international-ciat/sample-earth-2026-co-gh/sample-earth-tree-crops.jpg)

## Files

| File | Country | Sampling Sites | Polygons count| Points count | Imagery date range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ghana.gpkg` | Ghana | 258 | 6,277 | 13,366 | 2021-12-18 – 2025-11-23 |
| `colombia.gpkg` | Colombia | 147 | 6,672 | 12,272 | 2020-10-13 – 2025-09-10 |

Both GeoPackages use the WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) coordinate reference system and are licensed under CC BY 4.0.

## Tables

Each GeoPackage contains four tables:

### `land-cover-legend`

Attribute table containing the land cover classification legend.

| `land_cover_id` | `name` | `description` |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Coffee | Plantation containing coffee and any other crops |
| 1 | Cocoa | Plantation containing cocoa and any other plots |
| 2 | Tree crops | Tree crops plantation (including bamboo) without coffee or cocoa |
| 3 | Seasonal agriculture | Seasonal agriculture |

### `sampling-area`

Point geometry layer representing the centre of each sampling area cell. Each cell defines a 600 m × 600 m area within which imagery interpretation was conducted.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fid` | Integer | Auto-increment primary key |
| `geom` | Point | Centre point of the sampling area cell |
| `cell_uuid` | Text | Unique identifier of the sampling area cell |
| `imagery_date` | Date | Date of the satellite imagery used for interpretation in this cell |

### `polygon-collection`

MultiPolygon geometry layer containing exhaustive land cover delineations within each sampling area. Around each selected sampling area centre, within the 600 m extent, all cocoa, coffee, tree crops (orchards/bamboo), and seasonal agriculture pixels were mapped as polygons. Therefore, any non-annotated pixel within a sampling area can be assigned to the remaining (other) land cover categories. In other words, the polygon collection represents a complete annotation of the target classes within each cell.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fid` | Integer | Auto-increment primary key |
| `geom` | MultiPolygon | Delineated land cover polygon |
| `sample_uuid` | Text | Unique identifier for this polygon sample |
| `cell_uuid` | Text | Foreign key linking to the corresponding `sampling-area` cell |
| `land_cover_id` | Integer | Land cover class (see `land-cover-legend`) |
| `shade_level` | Integer | Shade level of the plantation for coffee and cocoa (0: full sun, 1: low shade, 2: medium shade, 3: high shade) (where applicable) |
| `recently_planted` | Boolean | Whether the plot was recently planted |
| `comment` | Text | Optional free-text comment |
| `created` | Datetime | Timestamp of record creation |
| `updated` | Datetime | Timestamp of last update |

### `point-collection`

Point geometry layer containing GPS reference points interpreted from high-resolution satellite imagery, collected within a 600–1200 m square buffer around the sampling area centre for each land cover category. These points complement the polygon collection by providing point-based reference samples across the classified categories.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fid` | Integer | Auto-increment primary key |
| `geom` | Point | Point location of the sample |
| `sample_uuid` | Text | Unique identifier for this point sample |
| `cell_uuid` | Text | Foreign key linking to the corresponding `sampling-area` cell |
| `land_cover_id` | Integer | Land cover class (see `land-cover-legend`) |
| `shade_level` | Integer |  Shade level of the plantation for coffee and cocoa (0: full sun, 1: low shade, 2: medium shade, 3: high shade) (where applicable) |
| `recently_planted` | Boolean | Whether the plot was recently planted |
| `comment` | Text | Optional free-text comment |
| `created` | Datetime | Timestamp of record creation |
| `updated` | Datetime | Timestamp of last update |

## Visualisation

A QGIS project is provided to visualise the dataset with pre-configured styling and layer ordering. Open the `.qgz` project file in [QGIS](https://qgis.org/) (version 3.x or later) to explore the data with the appropriate symbology and basemap.

## Collecting new samples: QGIS form setup

If you'd like to collect additional points and have them validate cleanly against the legend, configure the attribute form of `point-collection` (or `polygon-collection`) so that `land_cover_id` is picked from a drop-down sourced from `land-cover-legend`.

1. Right-click `point-collection` → Properties → Attributes Form.
2. In the field list on the left, select `land_cover_id`.
3. Change Widget Type to **Value Relation** and set:
   - **Layer**: `land-cover-legend`
   - **Key column**: `land_cover_id` (the integer stored in the point)
   - **Value column**: `name` (the label shown to the surveyor)
   - **Allow NULL value**: leave unchecked (every point must have a class)
   - **Order by value**: ✓
4. Recommended widgets for the other fields:
   - `sample_uuid`, `cell_uuid`: *Text Edit*, with a default expression of `uuid()` for `sample_uuid` and a Value Relation to `sampling-area.cell_uuid` for `cell_uuid`.
   - `shade_level`: *Range* (Integer, min 0 max 3) or a Value Map if you have fixed categories.
   - `recently_planted`: *Checkbox*.
   - `created`, `updated`: *Date/Time*, with default expression `now()` and, for `updated`, **Apply default value on update** ticked.
   - `comment`: *Text Edit*, multi-line.
5. Project → Save to persist the form configuration in the project file.

With this setup, opening the **identify → form** view on a new point gives surveyors a drop-down of legend names rather than raw integers, while the stored value remains the integer `land_cover_id`. This keeps the file consistent with the existing data and the schema documented above.

## Sampling Methodology

1. **Sampling area selection:** Sampling area centres were randomly drawn from known coffee and cocoa production areas in each study region, so that the sampled cells are concentrated where the target commodities occur.
2. **Imagery interpretation:** For each cell, high-resolution satellite imagery (date recorded in `imagery_date`) was used as the basis for visual interpretation.
3. **Polygon mapping:** Within a 600 m extent around each sampling area centre, all pixels corresponding to cocoa, coffee, tree crops (orchards/bamboo), and seasonal agriculture were exhaustively delineated as polygons. Non-annotated pixels within these areas can therefore be considered as belonging to other land cover types.
4. **Point sampling:** Reference GPS points were identified from high-resolution satellite imagery within a square buffer extending 600–1200 m around each sampling area centre to generate the point-collection layer.

## Using these data in another QGIS project

You can reuse the GeoPackages directly in your own QGIS project. Simply drag each `.gpkg` into the **Browser** or use **Layer → Add Layer → Add Vector Layer…**. Each file exposes its four tables as separate layers: `land-cover-legend`, `sampling-area`, `polygon-collection`, and `point-collection`.

### Joining with the legend

**QGIS join:** this makes the legend's `name` and `description` appear as virtual fields on every polygon/point feature in the attribute table and identify tool.

1. Add all four layers from the GeoPackage to your project: `land-cover-legend`, `sampling-area`, `polygon-collection`, `point-collection`.
2. In the **Layers** panel, right-click `polygon-collection` → **Properties → Joins**.
3. Click the **green +** at the bottom and configure:
   - **Join layer**: `land-cover-legend`
   - **Join field**: `land_cover_id`
   - **Target field**: `land_cover_id`
   - **Cache join layer in memory**: ✓ (faster lookups)
   - **Custom field name prefix**: clear it (or set to `legend_`) so columns appear as `name`/`description` instead of `land-cover-legend_name`.
   - Optionally tick **Joined fields** and select only `name` and `description`.
4. Repeat the same join on `point-collection`.
5. **Project → Save** so the joins are stored in your `.qgz` project file.

The joins are saved in the QGIS project, not in the GeoPackage, so the `.gpkg` files remain unchanged and portable.

## Get Involved

We are actively looking for collaborators to expand this dataset to new geographies and crop types. If you are a researcher, practitioner, or organisation working on land cover mapping, remote sensing, or agricultural monitoring and would like to contribute, whether by collecting new reference data, validating existing annotations, or integrating this dataset into your workflows, we would love to hear from you. Please reach out to us at **T.Vantalon@cgiar.org**.
